MISSION VIEJO MINUTES
  City Council, Community Development Financing Authority,
  Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency,
  Housing Authority, and Library Board of Trustees*

  May 27, 2025
A Regular Meeting of the City Council, the Community Development Financing Authority, the
Successor Agency of the Community Development Agency, the Housing Authority, and the Library
Board of Trustees of the City of Mission Viejo, California, was called to order by Mayor Ruesch at
5:01 p.m., on May 27, 2025, at 200 Civic Center, Mission Viejo, California.

A complete copy of the agenda for the meeting containing all items as shown herein was posted by
5:00 p.m. on May 22, 2025, on the outdoor bulletin board at City Hall. A copy was also posted at
the Montanoso Recreation and Fitness Center, 25800 Montanoso Drive and Norman P. Murray
Community and Senior Center, 24932 Veterans Way.

*All Board and Agency memberships are reflected in the title "Council Member."

Present:  Council Member Goodell
  Council Member Kelley
  Council Member Vasquez
  Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum
  Mayor Ruesch

Absent:  None

Staff Present:  Elaine Lister, City Manager
  Jerry Hill, Assistant City Manager
  William P. Curley, City Attorney
  Ellis Chang, Director of Administrative Services
  Kimberly Schmitt, City clerk
  Renata Winter, Assistant City Clerk

CLOSED SESSION

CS1. Conference with Legal Counsel - Existing Litigation Paragraph (1) of subdivision (d) of
  Section 54956.9 Janice Kronik Gath, et. al v. Mission Viejo OCSC Case No. 30-2024-
  01376969-CU-MC-CJC

CS2. Conference with Real Property Negotiators - Property: 25282 Marguerite Parkway,
  Mission Viejo, Ca 92692; Agency Negotiators: City Manager Elaine Lister, Assistant
  City Manager Jerry Hill, City Attorney William P. Curley III, Director of
  Administrative Services/City Treasurer Ellis Chang. Negotiation Parties: Kathleen
  Sickles, Property Representative. Under negotiation: terms of payment.

City Council Minutes  1  May 13, 2025
 RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION AND RECONVENE

At the hour of 5:01 Mayor Ruesch recessed to Closed Session. At the hour of 6:01 Mayor Ruesch
reconvened the meeting with all five Council Members present.

REPORT OF CLOSED SESSION

City Attorney Curley announced that there were no reportable actions for CS1 and CS2.

INVOCATION: Council Member Vasquez

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE: Council Member Goodell

PRESENTATIONS

P1. Proclaim May through August 2025 as Drowning Prevention & Awareness Season

  Presented proclamation to Fire Chief Cheyne Maule.

P2. Presentation to the City by the Veterans of Foreign Wars (VFW)

  VFW Post 6024 Commander, John Carson and VFW Post 6024 Adjutant, Ned Costa
  presented certificates to Deputy Brandon Espinosa, Mayor Bob Ruesch, and Director of
  Recreation and Community Services, Mark Nix.

PUBLIC COMMENTS

Rob Sullivan, M.V.: Asked if there is a possibility of having the dog park parking lot asphalted in
the future.

Kristen Wilcox, M.V.: Asked that the police blotter be brought back. Expressed concerns about
the police budget.

Natalie Winter, M.V.: Thanked the Council for their support of the Mission Viejo Girl’s softball
League as well as staff members.

CONSENT CALENDAR

Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to approve the
Consent Calendar outlined below.

On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
NOES:  None
ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  2  May 13, 2025
 1.  City Council Minutes

  Approved the Minutes for the regular City Council Meeting of May 13, 2025, as presented.

2.  General Check Register Dated May 2, 2025, in the Amount of $1,130,771.03

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

3.  General Check Register Dated May 9, 2025, in the Amount of $3,269,676.41

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

4.  Golf Check Register Dated May 2, 2025, in the Amount of $72,518.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

5.  Golf Check Register Dated May 9, 2025, in the Amount of $273,146.20

  Ratified the accompanying check register.

6.  Consultant Services for Coordination of Activities at Mission Viejo Television (MVTV)

  (1) Awarded a contract to Eric Winter (A25-14) for coordination of activities at Mission Viejo
  Television for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2027, in the amount of $67,036.64;
  and (2) authorized staff to issue a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2025,
  through June 30, 2026, in the amount of $32,384.85 pending adoption of the Fiscal Year 2025-
  27 budget by the City Council.

7.  Consultant Services for Producer/Director of Various Mission Viejo Television
  Programs

  (1) Awarded a contract for the subject services to Eric Winter (A25-15) for the period of July
  1, 2025, through June 30, 2027, in the amount of $190,639.28; and (2) authorized issuance of
  a purchase order to Eric Winter for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, in an
  amount not to exceed $93,441.46 pending adoption of the FY 2025-27 budget by the City
  Council.

8.  Maintenance Of Traffic Signals and Appurtenance, Interconnect, Battery Back-Up
  Systems, Illuminated Street Name Signs, Safety Lights, CCTV Cameras, Speed
  Feedback Signs and Illuminated Crosswalk Services - Second & Third Contract
  Amendments

  (1) Approved Contract Amendment #2 with Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc. to increase the
  current purchase order for Fiscal Year 2024-2025 in the amount of $66,000 and (2) approved
  Contract Amendment #3 with Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc. for Fiscal Year 2025-2026 to
  modify certain terms of the contract contingent upon approval of the Fiscal Year 2025-2027

City Council Minutes  3  May 13, 2025
   budget and (3) authorized the issuance of a purchase order to Bear Electrical Solutions, Inc.
  for the period from July 1, 2025 through June 30, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $500,000.

9.  2025 Fourth of July Community Street Faire

  Approved the Special Events Permit submitted by the Mission Viejo Activities Committee
  authorizing the annual Mission Viejo Fourth of July Community Street Faire on Friday, July
  4, 2025.

10. City of Mission Viejo Renewed Measure M (M2) Eligibility: MPAH Consistency and
  Mitigation Fee Program Components

  (1) Adopted Resolution 25-18 Concerning the Status and Update of the General Plan
  Circulation Element and Mitigation Fee Program for the Renewed Measure M (M2) Program,
  and (2) directed staff to transmit said resolution to the Orange County Transportation
  Authority by June 30, 2025, to maintain the City's continued eligibility in receiving
  FY2025/26 M2 local fair share revenues and in pursuing competitive grant funding
  opportunities.

11. Revisions to the Norman P. Murray Community Center Facility Regulations, Sports
  Field Use and Allocation Policy, and the City Council’s Special Event Policy

  (1) Approved revisions as recommended by the Community Services Commission to the
  Norman P. Murray Community Center Facility Regulations, Sports Field Use and Allocation
  Policy, and the City Council's Special Event Policy, and (2) adopted Resolution 25-19
  Amending the Council's Special Event Policy and the City Council Policy Manual.

12. Professional Services Agreement for Printing and Related Services for the "Mission
  Viejo Life" Publication

  (1) Approved the Professional Services Agreement with Advantage Inc. (A25-16) for printing
  and related services for up to eight issues of Mission Viejo Life in the amount of $193,379.32
  for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2027; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase
  order to Advantage Inc. for the period of July 1, 2025, through June 30, 2026, in an amount
  not to exceed $95,269.64.

13. Request for a One-Time Exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  Regulation at City Facilities for a Community Event

  Approved the request for a one-time exemption to the "No Alcoholic Beverage Consumption"
  Regulation at City facilities for the Mission Viejo Barbecue Music Fest event.

14. Annual Routine Janitorial Supplies at City Facilities

  (1) Awarded contract to Waxie Sanitary Supply (A25-17) for Annual Routine Janitorial
  Supplies at City Facilities for the period of June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2027, in the amount not
  of $330,000; and (2) authorized issuance of a purchase order to Waxie Sanitary Supply for
City Council Minutes  4  May 13, 2025
   the period of June 1, 2025 to May 31, 2026, in an amount not to exceed $165,000, pending
  adoption of the 2025-2027 budget by City Council.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

15. State Fire Marshals 2025 Recommended Fire Hazard Severity Zones (FHSZ) Maps

  Director of Community Development Larry Longenecker and Planning & Economic
  Development Manager Cliff Jones presented the staff report.

  The Mayor Ruesch opened the Public Hearing at 6:55 pm

  Paula Murray, M.V.: Voiced concerns that she had only recently heard of this and she lives
  in the high fire area and questioned why residents didn’t hear about this sooner. She suggested
  that we utilize the Wilderness Glen area similar to the Oso Creek.

  Jeff Kasper, M.V.: Asked if the efforts to mitigate the vegetation to make it less hazardous
  will lower the risk for the next five years.

  David Collins, M.V.: Voiced his concerns about the open space in the north end of the City
  and expressed his gratitude to the Council and staff and Fire Authority for moving this effort
  forward.

  Kenny Dossey, M.V.: Looked at the plan as a retired fire fighter that this bogus. Questioned
  if the Council has any say in this.

  Ralph Bobson, M.V.: Voiced his concerns that insurance companies are going to cancel or
  raise premiums based on this map.

  Mayor Ruesch closed the Public Hearing at 7:05 pm

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Mayor Ruesch, to introduce
  Ordinance 25-355 Adopting and designating the State Fire Marshals 2025 recommended
  Local Responsibility Area Fire Hazard Severity Zones (FHSZ) maps, without revisions,
  pursuant to California State Law and Related Findings.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

City Council Minutes  5  May 13, 2025
 NEW BUSINESS

16. Fiscal Year 2025-2026 Law Enforcement Agreement and Additional Special
  Enforcement Services Provided by the Orange County Sheriff’s Department (OCSD)

  Emergency Operations Manager Paul Catsimanes presented the staff report.

  Motion made by Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum, seconded by Council Member Kelley, to (1)
  approve the FY 2025-2026 Law Enforcement Services Agreement with the County of Orange
  (A25-18) for an amount not to exceed $25,543,492; and (2) approved funding in FY 2025-26
  in the amount not to exceed $35,000 for overtime related to special enforcement services.

  On roll call, said motion carried by the following vote:

  AYES:  Bucknum, Goodell, Kelley, Ruesch, and Vasquez
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None

MAYOR’S, COMMISSION, COMMITTEE REPORTS AND ACTIONS

17. Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG) Report

  Received written report.

COUNCIL MEMBER COMMENTS AND ACTIONS

18. Council Member Reports of Events and Activities Attended ~ AB1234

By consensus, the City Council Members acknowledged their event and activities calendars as
presented in the report and agreed to provide any changes to the City Clerk for the public record.

Council Member Goodell

Council Member Goodell reported that the National Olympic Committee was in Los Angeles this
past week and that several of them came to Mission Viejo for tours of our facilities. He stated he
met with the Netherlands and worked out the details of an agreement and that Finland had a
successful tour last Friday so they may be coming to train in our city.

Council Member Kelley

Council Member Kelley commended our city staff for their efforts in planning a wonderful
Memorial Day Ceremony honoring our fallen and veterans. She stated she attended a press
conference calling for the bipartisan legislative reforms to alcohol and drug treatment facilities
which Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum was one of the speakers. It was very encouraging to hear the
support to have this forum. Council Member Kelley mentioned that she attended the Love Mission
Viejo Day on May 17 and expressed the great turnout of volunteers that showed up and commended
those that planned the event. Lastly, she announced that both school districts are out for the summer
City Council Minutes  6  May 13, 2025
 on June 5 and encourage residents to look at the many classes and camps that the City provides at
our various facilities.

Council Member Vasquez

Council Member Vasquez attended the Capo Valley High School Senior Awards and stated that
her daughter will be graduating next week. She reported that the girl scout troop she co-leads went
rock climbing and had a great time. Council Member Vasquez also attended the Memorial Day
Service. She attended the Interact Club Banquet at Capo Valley High School. She promoted the
BMX Bike Show at the Shops at Mission Viejo this coming Saturday and later in the day she will
be attending a Naxolene workshop where they will be handing out free Narcan.

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum

Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum highlighted the press conference on sober living homes. She gave
kudos to The League of California Cities their participation. She stated that Love Mission Viejo
Day was great, and she was very honored to have been on the original planning committee for this
event. Mayor Pro Tem also mentioned the 80’s themed Nigh Market and what a great evening of
great music and food. She attended and Eagle Scout Court of Honor on behalf of the Mayor and
complimented staff on a great Memorial Day service. Highlighted our law enforcement is very
proactive in preventative homelessness and explained how we are ahead of the curve compared to
a lot of other cities. She reminded residents of the Paws Creek Golf Tournament this upcoming
weekend and that the Friends of the Library will be hosting their summer book sale June 6 and 7.
Lastly, she announced that the Montanoso and Sierra Recreations Centers will be holding an open
house on June 7 noon to 4 pm.

Mayor Ruesch

Mayor Ruesch and Mayor Pro Tem Bucknum attended the Foutain Valley Crawdad Festival where
they were introduced to the promoters to look into holding a barbecue contest this summer in
Mission Viejo. He stated this past Saturday he had the privilege to present the Mayor’s Trophy at
the chili cook-off. He commented on the juveniles that participated and had incredible chili. He also
attended the Love Mission Viejo Day. Lastly, he closed with the following quote, “We enter as
individuals, we work as a team, and we leave as a family”.

ADJOURNMENT

At the hour of 7:43p.m., with no further business to come before the City Council at this session,
Mayor Ruesch adjourned the meeting to Tuesday, June 10, 2025, at 5:00 p.m.

______________________________________
Kimberly Schmitt, City Clerk

Approved at the meeting of June 10, 2025

City Council Minutes  7  May 13, 2025
